name: Limewashed
process: The surface is dampened (not wet), then limewash is scrubbed and worked in thinly with a large, rough brush. At least three or four coats are built up, each dried and the surface dampened again before the next. Laid thin it carbonates to a sound calcite skin; laid thick it crazes. Outdoors it is renewed about every five years, so an old wall carries many generations of coats.

steps.step: wet the surface with clean cold water and leave it until damp but not wet
steps.source: Bennett, B. (1997) Awash with Colour: The Decorative and Protective Roles of Limewash. The Building Conservation Directory, https://www.buildingconservation.com/articles/decorative-protective-limewash/decorative-protective-limewash.htm

steps.step: apply thinly and work in well with a large, rough-textured brush (scrubbed in with a circular motion)
let each coat dry, dampen, and apply the next

crazingWhenThick.text: crazing occurs when it is applied more liberally

gypsumSubstrate.text: gauging a lime finish with gypsum can vary its suction and affect the appearance of limewash and distemper laid over it
gypsumSubstrate.source: Napier, W. & Jenkins, M. (2018) Inform Guide: Plain Lime Plastering. Historic Environment Scotland, https://www.historicenvironment.scot/archives-and-research/publications/publication/?publicationId=67d4d72c-7b8c-4622-a244-a94b01090177

surface.matt: Dead matt: the carbonated film is a fine porous calcite layer with no binder skin.
surface.strokes: Brush marks and slight differences of opacity between strokes; the substrate's texture shows through.
surface.buildUp: Generations of coats round over arrises and fill fine relief.
surface.drying: Semi-transparent and darker while wet; dries many shades lighter and opaque.

photograph: Uneven, soft, chalky white with visible brushwork; the trowelled plaster below shows through thin places.
A fine craze where a coat went on thick.

unverified.reason: No measured film thickness per coat was found.

sources: Bennett, B. (1997) The Building Conservation Directory.
Napier, W. & Jenkins, M. (2018) Inform Guide: Plain Lime Plastering. Historic Environment Scotland.
